e2ae95ed-9033-5625-9179-33f4cf4a95c1.content: Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.

4be60357-09fa-523d-8c8d-8e03ace8fde9.content: Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.

0dd5d707-7d13-5be0-8377-421507650cba.content: Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.

9b3f0cde-7c3e-5b6a-9500-855f31d65ef2.content: Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.

8c896114-85e6-5c3c-ae3f-6e8e6b59f2fe.content: Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.

dc9e3f25-7aac-500b-b431-f6d810dd09bb.content: When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.

04956cab-eb3a-5b71-be45-b1edd6c4a216.content: Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.

fc8613e8-86ca-5322-bb5d-03dfbca71c46.content: The user writing this proposal tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”
